items.query_text: When the Cursor hook wrapper form changes between installs (sh versus cmd.exe), a non-force reinstall leaves the stale hook entry in place and adds the new one, creating a duplicate that can double-fire and produce duplicate checkpoints. Replace any existing Entire hook of that type regardless of wrapper form when the desired command changes, without requiring --force, while preserving non-Entire entries.

label_evidence.rationale: The retained packet placed fact:30c6c2e4a031d91df16e4d27 first; exact text was matched back to the pinned full fact corpus before grading.

judgments.rationale: It states the required stale Entire-managed wrapper replacement rule and the sh/cmd.exe migration behavior directly.
It concerns ownership-safe hook replacement, but for Copilot commands rather than Cursor wrapper-form migration.
Avoiding duplicate checkpoint database rows is unrelated to replacing installed hook entries.

items.query_text: How should an Entire-managed Cursor hook be migrated when reinstalling changes its wrapper between sh and cmd.exe?

label_evidence.rationale: This oracle wording names the exact wrapper migration represented by the retained packet's first fact.

judgments.rationale: The fact is an exact answer to the oracle query.
It describes duplicate lifecycle hooks, but the cause is cross-agent dispatch rather than wrapper-form migration.
A Git operations package boundary does not answer hook migration behavior.

items.query_text: Pi review token accounting double-counts cache token usage in the event stream. Make cache token counts accumulate correctly instead of being counted twice.

label_evidence.rationale: The retained packet supplied token-accounting invariants; exact packet text was mapped to pinned corpus fact IDs before grading.

judgments.rationale: It establishes cumulative event-stream token accounting, a useful analogue for Pi's cumulative cache-token handling, without specifying Pi's event shape.
It is strongly topical to cache-token double counting but describes Codex inclusive fields rather than Pi stream accumulation.
Its double-counting issue concerns recap contributors and API data sources, not reviewer token events.

items.query_text: When origin (or the push remote) is an entire:// mirror URL whose forge matches the configured checkpoint remote provider, checkpoint push falls back to direct SSH/HTTPS against the provider host instead of going through the mirror on the same cluster. Derive the checkpoint URL on that cluster for the matching case, keeping the provider-host fallback for file:// and forge-mismatched mirrors and when a checkpoint token forces provider HTTPS.

label_evidence.rationale: Human review compared the exposed task prompt with eligible facts proposed from the pinned corpus; no agent memory packet was retained for this no-memory development run.

judgments.rationale: It establishes that checkpoint URL/auth derivation follows the active push remote, which is central context, but does not state same-cluster entire:// derivation.
It correctly covers the token-forces-HTTPS exception but not mirror-cluster routing in the tokenless matching-forge case.
Local checkpoint discovery has no bearing on remote URL derivation.

items.query_text: Checkpoint resume auto-detection fails to resume work whose branch only exists on origin: when a target matches no checkpoint, local branch, or commit, it gives up instead of offering to fetch the remote branch. Add a remote-branch fallback, tried only after commit resolution so revision syntax like HEAD isn't misrouted.

label_evidence.rationale: The retained packet contains no direct solution, while exposed full-corpus review found a branch-oriented remote-resume contract that is useful context. Without exhaustive active-corpus closure this query is not labeled null.

judgments.rationale: It establishes that remote resume is branch-oriented via `entire resume <branch>`, useful context for a remote-branch fallback, but does not specify target-resolution ordering or fetching.
It mentions a deliberately omitted remote-tracking fallback, but for the local-only v1.1 metadata mirror rather than resume target resolution.
It discusses branch/push remote resolution, but for policy refs rather than checkpoint resume auto-detection.
Trail branch ownership does not address resolving a resume target.

items.query_text:
In a checkpoint-enabled clone, plain git maintenance commands have started misbehaving: `git fetch --all` and `git remote update` now try to contact every checkpoint URL the repository has ever fetched from - including long-dead mirror hosts and internal SSH URLs - which makes those bulk commands slow and prone to hard errors when any of those hosts is unreachable.

The cause traces back to how Entire pulls checkpoints: each filtered checkpoint fetch appears to leave its own `remote.<url>.*` section behind in the clone's `.git/config`, and git then treats each of those sections as just another fetchable remote, so `--all` / `remote update` dial all of them.

Make bulk fetch/update operations stop reaching out to these accumulated per-checkpoint entries. The constraint: normal on-demand object fetching for filtered checkpoints (pulling in objects that were filtered out at fetch time) must keep working exactly as before, and a normal unfiltered fetch must not start leaving new config sections behind either. Only the bulk-fetch behavior should change.

label_evidence.rationale: The exposed prompt and eligible facts contain the exact synthetic-promisor mechanism, while the named-remote rejection is counterevidence rather than a solution to bulk-fetch participation.

judgments.rationale: It rejects named-remote filtered fetches and prescribes URL fetches, but URL fetches create the synthetic promisor entries that this task must exclude from `fetch --all` and `remote update`; it does not solve that behavior.
It explains that literal URL/path fetches can still persist synthetic promisor sections, the exact mechanism behind bulk-fetch exposure.
It concerns legacy origin pollution and cleanup, not suppressing accumulated literal-URL remotes during bulk fetch/update.
Trail PR base synchronization is unrelated to Git promisor configuration.

items.query_text: Running `entire enable` imports agent session history as a side effect. In a non-interactive context (script, pipe, or no TTY) it imports history for all eligible agents with no confirmation, and it can import history that the repository configuration should not allow — behaving differently from the standalone import command in that respect. Make enable's history-import behavior safe and consistent with standalone import. Keep the fix minimal.

label_evidence.rationale: This task was already retrieval-probed; manual review found an eligible fact that records removal of automatic enable-time import prompting.

judgments.rationale: It states the safe product rule directly: imports are explicit manual commands rather than an enable-time side effect.
It specifies non-interactive enable behavior, but does not establish repository-policy validation for history imports.
A Go import cycle in token usage code does not affect enable-time history import.

items.query_text: The API client follows redirects with the default client and re-adds the Authorization header on every hop, so a backend redirect to another host, or a path that resolves cross-host, carries the Entire bearer token off-origin. Reject any request whose resolved host differs from the API base host and refuse cross-host redirects, so the token only ever goes to the API's own host. Also make the logged-out path return a normal error so the login hint prints.

label_evidence.rationale: Manual review found security invariants that constrain bearer-token destinations, but no fact that describes this API client's redirect callback implementation exactly.

judgments.rationale: It establishes that a raw token may only be sent to a validated HTTPS origin, useful security guidance for rejecting off-origin redirects.
It is about cross-host auth redirects, but the failure is device-grant store separation rather than Authorization-header leakage.
Bearer expiry during recap does not address redirect host validation.

items.query_text: In cluster discovery, a pre-audience cache entry forces a re-fetch, and if that fetch fails the stale audience-less entry is returned, so the git path misdiagnoses a transient discovery failure as 'this cluster predates jurisdiction-token git auth'. For audience-requiring callers, exclude pre-audience entries from the discovery-failure fallback so the real error surfaces; cores-only callers shouldn't force a re-fetch on fresh audience-less entries at all.

label_evidence.rationale: The eligible corpus contains the stale-cache fallback policy and separate cache architecture needed to judge this discovery regression.

judgments.rationale: It directly distinguishes expired-entry fallback from the hard error required when no usable entry exists.
It describes discovery cache structure and TTL, but not audience-aware fallback eligibility.
An expired recap token is unrelated to cluster-core discovery fallback.

items.query_text: The cleanup/clean flow flags imported sessions as orphaned and removes them, even though they were legitimately imported. Imported sessions should never be treated as orphans during cleanup.

label_evidence.rationale: Manual review found separate eligible facts for imported-checkpoint constraints and strategy-owned orphan classification; neither was inferred from the prompt alone.

judgments.rationale: It establishes imported checkpoints as a distinct protected kind, supporting exclusion from destructive generic cleanup.
It is about preventing cleanup of legitimate session state, but for active carry-forward work rather than imported sessions.
Recap response completeness does not affect orphan classification.

items.query_text: Imported sessions are subject to the staleness auto-purge and get deleted once they age out, even though an imported session shouldn't expire that way. Exempt imported sessions from the staleness check so they're never treated as stale.

label_evidence.rationale: Manual review found an eligible imported-kind contract and a separate stale-session policy, allowing an honest partial-relevance judgment.

judgments.rationale: It defines imported checkpoints as a distinct kind that unsupported consumers must filter, relevant to exempting them from generic staleness consumers.
It defines stale ACTIVE display behavior, not imported-session lifetime or purge eligibility.
Fetching a metadata branch for explain is unrelated to session auto-purge.

items.query_text: The `trail` command's help text doesn't mention trail findings, so users don't discover them. Add a mention of trail findings to the trail help.

label_evidence.rationale: Eligible facts prove trail findings are a real user-facing workflow and provide both a relevant command contract and nearby help/discovery distractors.

judgments.rationale: It documents a concrete trail finding command and limitation, making findings relevant to the trail help surface without prescribing wording.
It addresses help as a discovery surface, but for experimental commands rather than trail findings.
Codex session registry behavior is unrelated to trail help.

items.query_text: Fanning out code search across mirror placements makes a mirrored repo return the same matches from its home and mirror cells; the merged result list is deduped but the stats are summed, so counts are inflated (for example '6 matches' for 3 unique results) and truncation is falsely reported. Dedupe the per-repo stats and subtract the duplicated portion from the totals, keeping per-cell truncation and zero-match repos intact.

label_evidence.rationale: No retained fact directly solves mirror-placement search statistics, but the corpus contains a cross-domain aggregation decision about eliminating double-counted contributors. Without exhaustive active-corpus closure this query is not labeled null.

judgments.rationale: It records replacing a parallel aggregator because it double-counted contributors and drifted totals, a useful cross-domain alternative for deduplicating aggregate statistics, though it does not specify mirror-cell search accounting.
It uses mirror metadata for API routing, not per-cell search-result deduplication.
Worktree shadow-branch scoping has no relationship to code-search statistics.
